key_insight: MUSE-Autoskill introduces a unified, memory-aware skill lifecycle (creation, memory, management, evaluation) that lets LLM agents continuously create, reuse, and refine modular skills, boosting long-term task-solving capability and reliability.
problem_solved: Existing skill creation methods treat skills as static, isolated artifacts, which limits reusability, robustness, and continual improvement; this work enables persistent, evolving skills for sustained agent performance.
method: Define a unified skill lifecycle (Creation → Memory → Management → Evaluation) to govern skill birth, storage, retrieval, and refinement.
Use memory-backed mechanisms to index, retrieve, and adapt skills across tasks so agents can compose and reuse prior competencies.
Automated evaluation and feedback loop to score skill utility and trigger refinement or retirement, enabling continuous self-improvement.
impact: Provides a practical framework for building agents that scale to complex, multi-step tasks by maintaining an evolving skill library—reducing redundancy and improving generalization and robustness across domains.
visual_elements: Lifecycle diagram illustrating Create → Memory → Manage → Evaluate loop with example skill transitions
Skill library cards showing metadata (usage count, success rate, version) and retrieval paths
Task-to-skill composition flowchart demonstrating how an agent assembles multiple skills to solve a complex task
Comparative chart showing task success and skill reuse growth over time versus static-skill baselines
paper_title: MUSE-Autoskill: Self-Evolving Agents via Skill Creation, Memory, Management, and Evaluation
paper_authors: Huawei Lin, Peng Li, Jie Song, Fuxin Jiang, Tieying Zhang
